question: Why was chat W4A4 WikiText-2 PPL 10.3263 vs paper ~5.9-6.1?
headline: 10.3263 is a bit-reproducible, correctly-measured (up to a documented metric-window difference) result of the configuration it actually ran: Llama-2-7b-CHAT, random-Hadamard seed-0 rotation, fake W4A4KV16, RTN+MSE-clip. It was never comparable to the paper number, which is Llama-2-7b BASE + LEARNED rotation.

quantified_decomposition.evaluator_note: prefix-32k subsample -0.0111 + BOS -0.0012 + harness residual ~-0.0003 (torchrun vs in-process ~2e-4, shared-token aggregation ~1e-4); loss math exact <=1e-4 (GATE B)
quantified_decomposition.pipeline_note: GATE D: 451/451 transformed weights bit-identical to official ptq_model; PPL 10.5254 vs 10.6272
quantified_decomposition.random_seed_effect: none: seed 0 BELOW the 10-seed chat median (10.63 vs median 11.04, range 10.43-12.95)
quantified_decomposition.rtn_vs_gptq: not a factor: released-code GPTQ is WORSE than RTN (chat 8.46, base 6.86); paper GPTQ 5.9 not reproducible from released code

corrected_values.caveat: rotation Cayley-optimized on wikitext-2 TRAIN with W4A4 in the loop (official recipe); wikitext PPL is in-distribution for the rotation. W4A16 with this rotation scores BELOW FP16 (6.30 vs 6.95) - a QAT-overfit signature. OOD check: the corrected MT-bench EAGLE matrix is statistically unchanged from the random-Hadamard control (max |dAL| 0.060).

eagle_al_consequence: Learned rotation does NOT materially change the 3x3 AL matrix (all |delta| <= 0.060, within cross-run noise except possibly T4_D16 +0.060); all prior AL conclusions stand with targets relabeled 'random-Hadamard control'.

gates.C: PASS via RTN 6.1972~paper 6.1; GPTQ release-code gap documented
